docs.title: Never type another invoice by hand.
docs.text:
Photo or forward an invoice or receipt, and it's read automatically, checked for arithmetic that doesn't add up, and queued for a quick human review — nothing reaches your accounting tool until you approve it.

Captures invoices from

Email WhatsApp Google Drive Dropbox + any photo or PDF

Pushes clean data to

QuickBooks Xero Google Sheets + your accounting tool Invoice arrives email, WhatsApp, or a drive folder → SnapTally reads it and checks the math adds up → You get a quick review with anything odd flagged → You approve it then it's ready for your books

Nothing is ever pushed to your accounting tool automatically — you always approve first.

Typing invoices by hand costs businesses a median of $21.40 per invoice once you count the labor — APQC's 2024–25 Open Standards Benchmarking data, as cited by accounts-payable software vendors. That's before counting the cost of the typos.

docs.title: The problem this solves
docs.text:
Someone on your team is still manually typing numbers off a photo or PDF into a spreadsheet or accounting software — vendor name, line items, totals, tax — one invoice at a time, usually at the end of a long day when mistakes are most likely.

  • It's slow by nature. Manual entry runs at roughly 4–5 invoices an hour once you count the interruptions, so a stack of invoices is a stack of lost hours, not a quick task.
  • Typos get buried until they cause a problem — a wrong total or a double-counted line item usually isn't caught until a payment is already wrong or a vendor calls asking where their money is.

SnapTally reads the invoice, checks that the numbers actually add up, and puts it in front of a human for a quick yes/no — instead of someone retyping every line by hand and hoping they didn't miss one.

Curious how it actually works under the hood? See how it works · set it up.

Cost-per-invoice figure: APQC's 2024–25 Open Standards Benchmarking data, as cited by AP automation vendors. Time-per-invoice figure: commonly cited AP benchmarking estimate (~4–5/hour). Both are industry benchmarks, not controlled studies — treat as directional.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: This page goes deep on purpose — it's the proof the homepage summary is real and tested, not just copy. You don't need to follow all of it to use the result.

docs.title: The flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  W[Invoice/receipt<br/>new document] -->|webhook + secret| AI[Extract with AI]
  AI --> P[Parse AI response]
  P --> E[Read existing invoice]
  E --> B[Build Review]
  B --> Q[Invoices sheet<br/>add or update]
  Q --> N[Email: review needed]

All the business rules live in one file, extract.js. build.js copies it into the workflow's Code nodes, so the rules that are tested are the same ones that run. The actual vision extraction (reading the image) happens in the Extract with AI node, calling Claude; everything after that is plain, testable logic.

docs.title: The math check
docs.text:
This is the trust layer: an invoice that "reads fine" but doesn't add up gets flagged instead of filed quietly.

Check Flag if it fails Line items sum to the stated subtotal (± rounding) Line items sum to $X but subtotal says $Y Subtotal + tax equals the stated total (± rounding) Subtotal + tax ($X) doesn't match the total ($Y)

Rounding tolerance is 2 cents, to absorb normal currency rounding without flagging every invoice.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Meaning Missing: vendor name, total amount The AI couldn't read a required field — usually a poor photo No line items extracted Nothing legible in the line-item area; check the image quality The two math-check flags above The numbers the AI read don't add up Figures changed since the last review – approval reset This invoice ID was re-extracted with a different vendor/subtotal/tax/total/currency than what's on record

A row is always written, flagged or not, so nothing silently disappears.

docs.title: When the same invoice comes in again
docs.text:
The workflow matches on the invoice number the AI extracted.

  • It updates the row rather than creating a duplicate.
  • The Status stays Approved only if the figures haven't changed. A re-send of the exact same invoice (e.g. a clearer photo) doesn't undo a review that already happened. But if the vendor, subtotal, tax, total or currency come back different — a corrected resend, a flaky re-scan, or someone resubmitting after approval — the row goes back to Needs review automatically. Approval never silently carries over a change to the actual numbers.

docs.title: What's real and what's sample
docs.text:
• Real: the validation/math-check logic and its tests (node extract.test.js); the n8n workflow structure.
  • Sample: every payload needs a real image/PDF URL and a working Anthropic credential to actually extract anything — the Node tests cover the logic layer by feeding it extraction results directly, the same way you'd mock any external AI/API call, not by running real images through the model.
  • One reviewer by default: this sends every review to a single configured address. Per-vendor or per-amount routing is the same Settings-sheet pattern CloseLoop and FirstReply use, just not built in yet.

docs.text: File What extract.js All rules: normalizing the AI's output, the math check, flags, review email extract.test.js Fixed-input checks for every rule (node extract.test.js) build.js Builds workflow.json with extract.js inlined into the Code nodes workflow.json Import into n8n (no credentials inside) payloads/, send-test.sh Sample intake payload and the script that sends it

docs.title: Set it up
docs.text:
You won't run any of this yourself if you hire me for it — this page is here so you (or your own dev team) can see exactly what's involved, and so there's a clean reference when I set it up for your account.

You need Docker and Node 18+, plus an Anthropic API key. Node is only used for the tests and build.js; n8n itself runs in Docker.

docs.title: 1. Run n8n locally
docs.text:
docker run -d --name n8n -p 5678:5678 -e GENERIC_TIMEZONE=Asia/Kolkata -e TZ=Asia/Kolkata -v n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n -v "$PWD:/files" docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n

Open http://localhost:5678 and create your login.

docs.title: 2. Google Sheet
docs.text:
Create a Sheet with one tab, Invoices, row 1 headers in this order:

Received at, Invoice ID, Vendor, Invoice date, Items, Subtotal, Tax, Total, Currency, Status, Flags
  • Give Status a dropdown: Needs review, Approved.
  • Format Received at as plain text (Format → Number → Plain text).

docs.title: 3. Credentials in n8n
docs.text:
• Anthropic API: add your API key as an HTTP Header Auth credential (header x-api-key), used by the Extract with AI node.
  • Google Sheets OAuth2 and Gmail OAuth2 (one OAuth client covers both; enable the Sheets, Drive and Gmail APIs): create an OAuth client in Google Cloud with redirect URI http://localhost:5678/rest/oauth2-credential/callback, then add the credential in n8n and sign in.
  • Webhook secret: create a Header Auth credential named Intake webhook secret, header name X-Intake-Secret, long random value. Copy .env.example to .env with the same value.

docs.title: 4. Build, import, publish
docs.text:
SHEET_ID=<sheet id> node build.js

docker exec n8n n8n import:workflow --input=/files/workflow.json && docker exec n8n n8n publish:workflow --id=snapTallyInvoices01 && docker restart n8n

Open the workflow and pick your credentials on the webhook node, the Anthropic HTTP node, both Google Sheets nodes, and the Gmail node. Then publish.

docs.title: 5. Try it
docs.text:
Replace the placeholder URL in payloads/new-invoice.json with a real public image/PDF URL of a sample invoice, then:

./send-test.sh payloads/new-invoice.json

A new row should appear in the Invoices sheet, and a review email should arrive. Try an invoice with an intentionally wrong total to see the math-check flag fire.

To run the rule tests (no image or API key needed, since these feed the logic layer directly): node extract.test.js should print extract ok.

docs.title: Going live with a real intake source
docs.text:
This is the one piece that's genuinely per-client, since "how does an invoice reach this workflow" varies:

  • Email attachment: an IMAP/Gmail trigger watching a dedicated inbox, saving the attachment and resolving a URL for it before calling Extract with AI.
  • WhatsApp: a Business Cloud API webhook on incoming media messages, same idea.
  • A Drive or Dropbox folder: a "new file" trigger on a dedicated upload folder.

Whichever it is, the only requirement reaching Extract with AI is a source_image_url it can fetch (public or signed). Everything downstream of that point is already built and tested.
